options.text: Both pieces gain weight, because a potato soaks up any liquid.
options.feedback: A fair idea, since a dry sponge does this. A potato is not a dry sponge: it is made of living cells full of water.

options.text: The piece in salt solution gains, because salt moves into it.
options.feedback: Many people expect this. The measurement goes the other way, and the salt does not cross the membrane of the cells.

options.text: The piece in plain water gains, and the piece in salt solution loses.
Neither changes, because potato cells are closed to water.
options.feedback: Water does cross the boundary of a cell, in both directions.
